recommend.rationale: Verdict: upheld (contradicted, as a tie). recommendAdmission: false. Pre-registration holds: protocol, ground truth and runner were committed in d12cb7783 (18:22:20Z) before the receipt (18:22:39Z) and the results commit 65f28dbd2, and the digests still match. An independent ast pass at d237c0839 reproduces all 27 ground-truth callers and the mechanical selection rule yields the same 5 targets from a pool of 128, so the targets were not hand-picked. Re-running the fixed runner reproduced both tool outputs byte for byte. Graphify and Graft return identical caller sets (recall 0.727/1.0/0.75/1.0/0.667, precision 22/22), so the challenger shows no caller-lookup advantage. Under the pre-registered rule a tie is contradicted, but it does not show Graft is better. The parser smoke test on non-target functions did not taint the result. The comparison is cross-bucket (Graphify is registered as safishamsi/graphify under knowledge-graph-build) and says nothing about Graphify's primary capability.

counterevidence.searched: Recomputed ground truth and target selection independently; re-ran runner/run-c1.py unchanged to check that the identical caller sets were not a runner duplication bug (separate graph.json vs graft CLI parse paths, per-target graft rawDigest present); looked for callers either tool found outside ground truth (none: both 22/22 precise).

items.summary: Both tools miss the same 5 of 27 callers (shadowEvaluation.py attribute/alias calls, the cardRenderer.py module-level comprehension, trustMagnitude._fusionAndSuiteOriginIds). This is a shared static-resolution limit, so the result is a tie rather than an incumbent advantage.
Graphify is already registered under knowledge-graph-build. Caller lookup on one Python package is a narrow slice of its claim, so this result does not bear on that bucket.

reexecution.notes: Re-ran runner/run-c1.py (sha256 96df20b5...) unchanged with graphify 0.8.13 and graft 0.25.0 at about 2026-10-28T18:35Z into a new path. native.json and graft.target.json came out byte-identical to the receipt outputs (sha256 942f1ec9fa9da6ac..., e556b0f8705c4186...) and the re-run scoring again reported contradicted with identical per-target recall. meta-verification-v1 rejects byte-identical artifacts as indistinguishable from copies, so those files are not listed and were not committed. Listed: the verifier's own ast ground-truth recomputation, which includes the script.

declaredSession.note: Separate session from the runner, dispatched by the same orchestrator, on the same host, account and Claude Code install. Declared, not authenticated; not environment-independent.

limitations: Five targets in one Python package at one revision; caller identity uses bare names.
C1 events.jsonl was edited after its results commit (commit reference corrected in 0c6cf9066, with the manifest updated). This is benign, but the log is not append-only.
Independence is declared and unauthenticated: the verifier was dispatched by the same orchestrator as the runner and ran on the same host, account and tool installs.
This record is an untrusted Meta assessment for human review. It is not an approval, an admission, a verification receipt or a Trust Magnitude, star, grade or Origin input.

Lead observedAtUTC/checkedAtUTC values in all four cases postdate the commits that contain them by roughly 8 to 10 hours (apparently local +08:00 times labelled Z, rounded). Git commit order, not those fields, was used to establish pre-registration.
events.jsonl entries were written in one batch at results-commit time (identical timestamps), so they are a summary, not a contemporaneous log.
